critical.name: --follow in _adder attributes ledger entries to foreign commits through inexact rename and copy detection
critical.summary: Both _adder functions now run `git log --follow --diff-filter=A` and take the last line. --follow pairs the followed path with any deleted or existing file that is at least 50% similar, and entry_text dumps every null field, so small entries (reopen, relink, rename, arm) share most of their lines. Verified at this head: `git log --follow --diff-filter=A HEAD -- docs/plans/freezes/skill/bookmark/r3.5-rename.json` returns f708dd8 (a strap-skills reopen) through R056 from add-bookmark/r3.1-reopen.json, then C074 from writing-docstrings, then C074 from strap-skills. The correct answer is 94d6961. The same query for the never-renamed writing-docstrings/r3.1-reopen.json returns f708dd8 where the old query returned e1cf2a7. As a result, the next `strap.py check bookmark` or ledger writer runs fg._reconcile_one and creates the annotated tag rename/skill/bookmark/r3.5-commit on f708dd8. Any new strap or plan entry that resembles an earlier file gets its -commit tag on an unrelated commit, and `check` prints wrong `untagged:` shas. freeze_git._adder serves plan ledgers too, and plan ledgers never move. tests/scripts/test_strap_rename.py does not catch this: its fixture ledger holds only a large freeze entry and it never asserts where the rename entry's commit tag points.
fix: Pin exact matches: add `-M100%` to both git log calls. At this head that returns 94d6961 for bookmark/r3.5-rename.json, 6b92205 for bookmark/r3.3-relink.json and e1cf2a7 for writing-docstrings/r3.1-reopen.json.

Drop --follow. Restore freeze_git._adder to `--diff-filter=A --reverse` and lines[0], since plans never rename. In strap_lock, look up an entry owned by an earlier name at `folder(owner)/entry_name(entry)` with the original query, and fall back to the current path. owners() already knows the old name.
Either way, add a rename test whose old ledger holds a reopen or relink entry, and assert that rename/<new stem>/rN.k-commit peels to the commit that added the rename entry.

important.name: rename leaves planned test node ids on the old file paths
important.summary:
_renamed moves the contract test, models, api and driver paths and anything under the old skill folder, and _renamed_behaviors rewrites statement and scenario text. Neither touches Behavior.tests[].node. When a mechanical behavior's planned test sits in a moved file (for example the contract test from named_paths), its node still names the old path. _planned_tests_pass (strap.py:937-941) then runs pytest on a file that no longer exists, the gate reports `planned tests fail`, and `freeze --refreeze` is refused. The spec is still frozen and sealed, so the node cannot be corrected without a reopen.

Also (overall): _renamed re-points the contract-test part (test_<old_snake>_skill_contract.py -> test_<new_snake>_...), but _renamed_behaviors only rewrites statement and scenario text; each mechanical behavior's tests[].node (e.g. tests/skills/test_c_msg_skill_contract.py::test_x) keeps the old file path, and the whole-word hyphen regex never matches the snake_case form anyway. freeze_problems -> _mechanical_gate -> _planned_tests_pass (strap.py:937-941) runs every node with pytest on the working tree, so after the contract test moves every such node fails with 'planned tests fail' and `freeze --refreeze` refuses. The node cannot be fixed afterwards: strap_api refuses behavior edits on a frozen spec, and after a reopen a behavior frozen in an earlier round keeps its tests (strap_api.py:215-226). Specs at the head pin 40+ nodes in contract tests (c-msg, merge-commit-msg, writing-docstrings, todo-edit, pr-sum, writing-comments), so renaming any of them strands the spec. The bookmark spec has no planned tests, which is why this PR's own run did not hit it. The planned-test mirror under the strap folder (tests/tests/skills/test_<old>_skill_contract.py) also keeps its old name.

Also (roast): _renamed_behaviors replaces every whole-word match of the old name in statements, task, tempts, check targets and judged subjects. The boundary only excludes [a-z0-9-], so a name that is also an English word gets rewritten in plain prose. This repo has skills named working, doctor and now bookmark. Renaming bookmark again would turn SC task text '... lists the bookmark goal subcommand' (SkillSpec.json line 251) into '... lists the <new> goal subcommand', and 'the working tree' would suffer the same fate under a working rename. save() then restamps the authored seal, so the edit is sealed without review. The command prints only a part count.

Also (adv_code_runtime): _renamed re-points the contract_test part from tests/skills/test_<old_snake>_skill_contract.py to the new name's path, and _rename_problems requires that new file to exist (so the old one is gone), but _renamed_behaviors rewrites only statement and scenario text; Behavior.tests[].node keeps the old file path. The next freeze --refreeze runs _mechanical_gate -> _planned_tests_pass, which runs pytest on the vanished node, so every mechanical behavior reports 'planned tests fail' and the renamed spec cannot refreeze; red/retest hit the same missing node. The word-boundary regex would not help either: node paths use the snake_case form, which the hyphenated pattern never matches.

Also (runtime): The swap pattern in _renamed_behaviors matches only spec.name with hyphens (add-bookmark). The models, api, driver and contract test paths that _renamed re-points through named_paths use the snake form (add_bookmark_api.py, test_add_bookmark_..._contract.py; strap_profile.py:35). So a statement or check target that names one of those files keeps the old module name, and the check then expects a file that has moved. The swap is also a plain whole-word replace: for a skill named with a common word, it rewrites prose and check regexes nobody asked to change, and prints no count.

Also (adv_code_runtime): _renamed re-points the models, api and driver parts (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/<old_snake>_api.py and so on), but the swap regex in _renamed_behaviors matches only the hyphenated name as a whole word. A file_changed/file_unchanged/path_present check whose target is one of those module paths keeps the old path, so after the rename the check watches a file that no longer exists (file_unchanged holds vacuously, file_changed/path_present can never hold).

Attack: Probe (run at PR head, output reproduced): build SkillSpec(name='old-one', mode='new', plugin_dir='plugins/harness', parts=[skill_md plugins/harness/skills/old-one/SKILL.md, contract_test tests/skills/test_old_one_skill_contract.py], behaviors=[Behavior(id='B1', kind='mechanical', tests=[PlannedTest(node='tests/skills/test_old_one_skill_contract.py::test_b1', red='AssertionError')])]) and call strap.py's _renamed(spec, 'new-one'). Result: parts == ['plugins/harness/skills/new-one/SKILL.md', 'tests/skills/test_new_one_skill_contract.py'] but behaviors[0].tests[0].node == 'tests/skills/test_old_one_skill_contract.py::test_b1'. End to end: freeze such a spec, git mv the skill folder and the contract test to the new name, run `strap.py rename old-one new-one` (succeeds), then `strap.py freeze new-one --refreeze` refuses with 'B1: planned tests fail' because pytest cannot find tests/skills/test_old_one_skill_contract.py.

Attack: Spec 'old-one' with a judgment behavior whose scenario has Check(kind='file_unchanged', target='plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/old_one_api.py') and an api part at that path. _renamed(spec, 'new-one') re-points the part to plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/new_one_api.py but leaves the check target at old_one_api.py: the pattern (?<![a-z0-9-])old\-one(?![a-z0-9-]) never matches 'old_one'.
fix: In _renamed_behaviors (or _renamed), rewrite each test as `test.model_copy(update={"node": _renamed_path(file, named, old, new) + "::" + rest})`, where file and rest come from `node.split("::", 1)`. Pass named, old and new through from _renamed. Add a rename test with a mechanical behavior whose node is in the contract test.

In _renamed_behaviors (or _renamed), re-point each behavior.tests[].node: split at '::', map the file part through the same `named`/_renamed_path mapping used for parts, and rejoin; rename the matching mirror files under the strap folder's tests/ in cmd_rename (inside the try, undone by _move_back).

Add a test in tests/scripts/test_strap_rename.py with a mechanical behavior whose planned node sits in the contract test, asserting the node is re-pointed and `freeze <new> --refreeze` passes the mechanical gate.
Limit the swap to name-bearing contexts (`harness:<name>`, `/<plugin>:<name>`, `skills/<name>/`, `strap/<name>/`, the profile's name-made paths) instead of every whole-word match

Or print each changed field (behavior id, scenario id, before -> after) in the rename output so the developer reviews the rewrite before refreezing, and cover a dictionary-word name in test_strap_rename.py

In _renamed_behaviors, rewrite each PlannedTest.node: split on the first '::', pass the file half through _renamed_path(path, named, old, new) and rejoin; extend _renamed to pass named/old/new through.
Add to _rename_problems a check that each renamed node's file exists, and a test in tests/scripts/test_strap_rename.py with a mechanical behavior whose node sits in the contract test.

Run a second swap for the snake form with the same boundaries, `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])old_snake(?![A-Za-z0-9_])`. Print the number of replacements per behavior in the rename summary so the developer can review them before the greens.
Apply _renamed_path (the named-path table) to each check target before the text swap, or add the snake_case old/new pair to the swap.

important.name: Rename rollback path (_move_back) has no test
important.summary:
`cmd_rename` moves the spec folder, saves the renamed spec and moves the ledger, then calls `sl.commit` inside a try. On failure, `_move_back` is supposed to put both folders back under the old name and restore the spec bytes. No test in test_strap_rename.py makes that block fail, so this undo of a half-done filesystem move is never run. Also, `sl.commit(root, pending)` gets no `restore`. Entries written before a failing write (the history entries of a legacy spec) stay in the folder that moves back, and no assertion checks for that.

Also (tests): `_rename_problems` refuses a part that is missing at its re-pointed path (strap.py:1148) and a new name whose spec folder already exists (strap.py:1151). The refusal tests cover an unmoved folder, an unfrozen spec, a locked spec, an existing ledger and a bad name, but not these two branches.

Also (roast): _move_back undoes a half-done rename with three conditional moves and a byte restore. No test in test_strap_rename.py drives a failure after the spec folder moved, so a regression here leaves a split tree: spec under the new name, ledger under the old name. The refusal tests all fail before anything moves. The refusal for a part missing at its new path is untested too.

Also (adv_code_tests): cmd_rename moves the spec folder and then, if save/move_ledger/commit fails, calls _move_back to restore both folders and the spec bytes. _rename_problems also refuses when the new name already has a spec folder. No test in tests/scripts/test_strap_rename.py reaches either path: the ledger-exists refusal test is refused in sl.rename_pending (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/strap_lock.py:312), before anything moves, so the rollback never runs under test.

Attack: Mutation: delete the `_move_back(spec.name, renamed.name, before)` call at plugins/harness/scripts/strap.py:1182, or delete the `_strap_dir(renamed.name).exists()` check at plugins/harness/scripts/strap.py:1150-1151, then run `python -m pytest tests/scripts/test_strap_rename.py -q`: all ten tests still pass (no other test in tests/ invokes `strap rename`).
fix: Add a test that monkeypatches `harness_lib.strap_lock._write_entries`, or `freeze_ledger.write_entry` for the rename kind, to raise `LedgerError`. Run `strap("rename", NAME, NEW)` and assert it is refused, `docs/PLANS/strap/demo-skill/SkillSpec.json` is byte-identical to before, the old ledger folder holds only its earlier files, and neither new-name folder exists.

important.name: No-other-agent guard now lets through any harness:bookmark* name
important.summary:
The renamed lookahead `harness:(?!bookmark)[a-z-]+` exempts every name that starts with `bookmark`, not just the skill itself. The old `(?!add-bookmark)` still caught `harness:bookmark-noter`, which is the deleted agent this file guards against (`_AGENT` at line 19). Since the rename, a SKILL.md body that dispatches `harness:bookmark-noter` again, or any `harness:bookmark-*` agent, passes `test_skill_body_names_no_agent_to_dispatch`. The only body mention today is `harness:bookmark` at SKILL.md:80, so a tighter pattern still passes.

Also (overall): test_skill_body_names_no_agent_to_dispatch asserts `re.search(r"harness:(?!bookmark)[a-z-]+", body) is None`. The negative lookahead now excludes every name that starts with 'bookmark', so a SKILL.md that dispatches `harness:bookmark-noter` (the very agent _AGENT at line 19 names and test_no_agent_runs_the_note_writer guards against) passes. Before the rename, `(?!add-bookmark)` let that reference fail the test; the rename silently weakened the guard for its most likely regression.

Also (roast): test_skill_body_names_no_agent_to_dispatch changed its lookahead from (?!add-bookmark) to (?!bookmark). The lookahead only checks the prefix, so any harness:bookmark<suffix> passes, including harness:bookmark-noter: the retired note-writer agent the same file pins as absent (_AGENT, line 19). Before the rename the old pattern caught it. The guard can no longer fail for the one agent it was written about.

Also (adv_code_tests): test_skill_body_names_no_agent_to_dispatch changed its exemption from (?!add-bookmark) to (?!bookmark). The lookahead is a prefix match, so any `harness:bookmark...` name passes, including `harness:bookmark-noter`, the agent the same file pins as removed (_AGENT, test_no_agent_runs_the_note_writer). Before the rename the old pattern caught `harness:bookmark-noter`; after it the guard misses the one agent name it most needs to catch.

Attack: Add the line `Dispatch harness:bookmark-noter to write the note.` to the body of plugins/harness/skills/bookmark/SKILL.md, then run `python -m pytest tests/skills/test_bookmark_skill_contract.py -q`: test_skill_body_names_no_agent_to_dispatch still passes. Directly: re.search(r'harness:(?!bookmark)[a-z-]+', 'dispatch harness:bookmark-noter') returns None, while the pre-PR pattern r'harness:(?!add-bookmark)[a-z-]+' matches it (a probe confirmed both results).
fix: Anchor the exemption to the whole name: `re.search(r"harness:(?!bookmark(?![a-z-]))[a-z-]+", body)`.
Alternatively, collect `re.findall(r"harness:([a-z-]+)", body)` and assert the set is a subset of `{"bookmark"}`.
Anchor the exclusion to the whole name: `re.search(r"harness:(?!bookmark(?![a-z0-9-]))[a-z0-9-]+", body) is None`.
Anchor the exception to the whole skill name: re.search(r"harness:(?!bookmark(?![a-z0-9-]))[a-z0-9-]+", body)
Or add an explicit assert "harness:bookmark-noter" not in body next to the regex
Anchor the exemption at the end of the name: re.search(r"harness:(?!bookmark(?![a-z-]))[a-z-]+", body)
Or collect every `harness:[a-z-]+` match and assert the set is a subset of {"harness:bookmark"}

minor.name: _rename_problems gives one misleading message for two separate conditions
minor.summary:
The condition at line 1146 is `old skill folder exists OR new SKILL.md missing`, and both cases print `<new>/SKILL.md does not exist; move ... first`. After a `git mv`, the old folder often survives holding only untracked or ignored leftovers such as commands/__pycache__ from running add_note.py. The rename is then refused with a message that says the new SKILL.md is missing when it exists.

Also (overall): _rename_problems joins two conditions into one message: when the old skill folder still exists (for example an untracked commands/__pycache__ that `git mv` leaves behind) and the new SKILL.md is present, the refusal still says '<new>/SKILL.md does not exist; move <old> to <new> first', pointing the developer at a file that is there.

Also (system_shape): plugins/harness/scripts/strap.py:1146-1147 ORs two conditions, `(root / old.skill_folder).exists() or not (root / new.skill_md).is_file()`, into one message: '<new skill_md> does not exist; move <old> to <new> first'. When the developer copies the folder instead of moving it (the new SKILL.md exists and the old folder is still there), the refusal says a file that exists does not exist. strap-skills/SKILL.md describes this refusal as 'a skill folder not yet moved', which only fits the second condition.
fix: Split the check into two problems: `<old folder> still exists; remove what remains there` when the old folder exists, and the current message only when the new SKILL.md is missing. Alternatively, test for tracked files under the old folder (`git ls-files`) instead of whether the folder exists.

Split the check: `if (root / old.skill_folder).exists(): problems.append(f"{old.skill_folder} still exists; move it to {new.skill_folder} (remove leftover untracked files)")` and `if not (root / new.skill_md).is_file(): problems.append(f"{new.skill_md} does not exist; move {old.skill_folder} to {new.skill_folder} first")`.
Split the check into two messages: '<old.skill_folder> still exists; move it to <new.skill_folder>' for the first condition and '<new.skill_md> does not exist; ...' for the second

minor.name: Rename refusal described as 'never frozen' but any unfrozen spec is refused

The command refuses a part missing at its new path (strap.py:1148-1149, `part ... does not exist`), so the contract test and the models/API/driver modules must move before the run. Read in order, the prose invites running the command first and hitting the refusal.

Move the sentence 'Move every part whose path is made from the name too: the contract test (...) and, for a harness skill, its models, API and driver modules.' ahead of the command, e.g. 'Move the skill folder first (`git mv`, then set the frontmatter `name`) and every part whose path is made from the name (...), on a frozen spec that is not Locked, then run'.

The state before is frozen, so the assertion state == frozen also passes if rename were mapped to frozen in _STATE_OF_KIND, which would wrongly re-freeze an armed or unlocked ledger.

Attack: Mutation: add `EntryKind.rename: LedgerState.frozen` to _STATE_OF_KIND in plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/freeze_ledger.py, then run `python -m pytest tests/lib/test_freeze_ledger.py -q`: test_rename_entry_names_the_old_subject_and_keeps_the_state still passes, because the only entry before the rename is a freeze.
fix: Precede the rename with an entry that leaves a state other than frozen (for example freeze, lock, unlock, or freeze, arm) and assert the state after the rename equals the state before it
